correctness.rationale: Exact anchoring of all real zero-sum loads reduces the 4m-dimensional quadratic form to A_p (m copies), S_p-C_p (m-1 copies), and M_m=S_p+(m-1)C_p (one copy). Determinants of A_p and S_p are strictly positive and their leading diagonals negative on 1<=p<p_c. The integral representation of (s+t)^p-s^p-t^p proves C_p strictly positive definite for 1<p<2, hence S_p-C_p<0. M_m(1)<0 and has a positive direction at p_c. The finite-metric strictness interval rules out any later return to negative type, giving one top-eigenvalue threshold and a one-dimensional endpoint kernel. Increasing m strictly increases M_m by C_p, proving strict decrease of thresholds. The first-order expansion of M_m at p=1 and the simple smaller root of det(S_1+t C_1′) give the sharp coefficient. Independently built graph distances and full spectral comparisons passed 1,993 supplementary assertions; these do not substitute for the proof.

value.rationale: Gluing copies of the simplest nontrivial odd cycle at a single cut vertex is a standard cactus construction and a structurally motivated test of preservation of negative-type exponents. Each petal individually has exponent p_c>1, whereas a many-petal bouquet has a genuinely new cross-petal obstruction, decreases strictly with the number of petals and approaches the tree-like exponent one at an exact rate. A complete all-m classification, critical equality dimension and first-order asymptotic are natural reusable metric-embedding invariants rather than arbitrary finite examples.
